previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and GERD was admitted for nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and left lower quadrant abdominal pain, with associated chest pain and dysuria. Symptoms were consistent with viral gastroenteritis, supported by normal white count, negative troponins, and resolution within 24 hours. A small amount of rectal bleeding was noted but stool testing was negative; likely due to hemorrhoids. Chest pain was non-ischemic and likely related to GI distress. Acute kidney injury, likely prerenal, resolved with hydration. All chronic medications were continued, with temporary hold of metformin. She improved clinically, was discharged home, and advised to follow up with her primary care provider for ongoing symptom evaluation.
